newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 7.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- The South African Chamber of Business (Sacob) has opposed the government's proposal to scrap the State Tender Board, arguing that the institution operated satisfactorily and should continue.

- The Chamber of Mines and National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) are embroiled in negotiations on the number of extra shifts needed to raise production by 90 tonnes of gold a year to ensure the industry's sirvival.
- Spoornet has bought a 20 percent share of Brazilian owned transport consortium Interferrea for an undisclosed amount.

- MPs are expected to get a 15 percent increase and cabinet ministers 12 percent, government sources have claimed, but presidential spokesman Parks Mankahlana would not confirm this, saying a decision was being processed.
- The Pathfinder mission's Mars rover was parked in the Martian dust for the night Sunday before starting its exploration of the planet after Earthrise.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Gold's precipitous fall over the past few days would push many local gold mines into deep financial trouble as the bullion price dipped below cash operating costs, analysts said at the weekend.

- Sugar industry employers and the five unions representing about 4,500 striking workers meet on Monday for a further round of wage talks amid allegations by sugar farmers that strikers have set fire to their farms.

- The South African Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (Satra) is to launch a nationwide crackdown on illegal callback operators, and could give Telkom the power to bar their telphone and fax numbers, sources said at the weekend.
- Portnet, the state-owned harbour operator, has lost its monopoly as the sole road transporter of goods moved to or from the area surrounding Durban harbour.

- Work has started on almost a quarter of the one million houses set as a target by the government to be built or be under construction by 1999, Housing Minister Sankie Mthembi-Mahanyele said at the weekend.
THE STAR

- World heavyweight champion Evander Holyfield received a hero's welcome at Johannesburg international airport on Sunday as scores of young fans jostled and heaved for a glimpse, or perhaps a lucky touch, of their boxing idol.
- Administrative bungles and the loss of cheques worth 450,000 rand by Gauteng health officials have left 500,000 Far East Rand people starving for the past three months.
- Police searching for a girl who disappeared on March 25, one day before testifying in a rape trial, have been sent on a wild goose chase by sangomas to whom they had turned for help.
- Thousands of drought-stricken farmers in landlocked Niger, one of the poorest and biggest countries in Africa, are caught up in a gold rush.
